articles.title: Timberland Bancorp 2026 Fiscal Year’s Net Income Increases 7% to $31.2 Million
articles.description: Fiscal Year EPS Increases 8% to $3.96Quarterly EPS Increases 6% to $1.04 from $0.98 for Preceding QuarterQuarterly Return on Average Assets Increases to 1.56%Quarterly Return on Average Equity Increases to 11.72%Quarterly Net Interest Margin Increases to 3.96%Quarterly Cash Dividend Increases 3% HOQUIAM, Wash., Oct. 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Timberland Bancorp, Inc. (NASDAQ: TSBK) ("Timberland” or "the Company”), the holding company for Timberland Bank (the "Bank”), today reported net income of $31.17 million for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026, an increase of 7% from $29.16 million for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025. Earnings per diluted common share ("EPS”) increased 8% to $3.96 for the 2026 fiscal year from $3.67 for the 2025 fiscal year. Timberland also reported net income of $8.11 million, or $1.04 per diluted common share for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. This compares to net income of $7.72 million, or $0.98 per diluted common share for the preceding quarter, and $8.45 million, or $1.07 per diluted common share, for the comparable quarter one year ago. (Note: net income for the comparable quarter one year ago was increased by a $1.04 million bank owned life insurance benefit claim.) "We closed out the fiscal year on a high note, delivering record annual earnings per share and a strong fourth quarter,” stated Dean Brydon, Chief Executive Officer. "Net income and earnings per share increased 5% and 6%, respectively, from the prior quarter, while net interest margin widened compared with both the prior quarter and year-ago quarter. While earnings were lower than the year-ago quarter, that period included a $1.04 million BOLI insurance claim, and excluding that benefit, results compared favorably. For the full fiscal year, we also improved our net interest margin and return on average assets while generating solid growth in net loans. We are proud of what our team accomplished this year in serving our customers, communities, and shareholders, and we look forward to building on that progress in the new year.” "As a result of Timberland’s strong earnings and capital position, our Board of Directors announced a 3% increase to the quarterly cash dividend to shareholders of $0.31 per share, payable on November 27, 2026, to shareholders of record on November 12, 2026,” stated Jonathan Fischer, President and Chief Operating Officer. "Marking our 56th consecutive quarterly cash dividend, this payment reflects the Board’s continued confidence in Timberland’s long-term prospects.” "Overall, fourth quarter earnings were strong and largely free of non-recurring items,” said Marci Basich, Chief Financial Officer. "Revenue generation was strong and net interest margin expanded 11 basis points from the prior quarter and 14 basis points from the year-ago quarter, reflecting our disciplined approach to pricing on both sides of the balance sheet. We also continued to build shareholder value during the quarter, growing tangible book value per share (non-GAAP) to $33.54, while repurchasing 40,395 shares of our common stock. These actions, combined with the dividend increase, reflect both the strength of our earnings and our confidence in the long-term value of the franchise.” "Net loans grew 2% from the prior quarter, a testament to the strength of our lending teams and the continued demand we are seeing in our markets,” Brydon continued. "Credit quality held steady with modest improvements in non-performing asset levels, delinquency levels, and substandard loan levels. While net charge-offs increased, that was largely the result of charging off specific reserves we had already set up on several loans in prior periods. Our markets continue to offer solid growth opportunities and we remain confident in the quality of our loan portfolio and our disciplined approach to credit risk management.” Earnings and Balance Sheet Highlights (at or for the periods ended September 30, 2026, compared to September 30, 2025, or June 30, 2026): Earnings Highlights: EPS increased 6% to $1.04 for the current quarter from $0.98 for the preceding quarter and decreased 3% from $1.07 for the comparable quarter one year ago;EPS increased 8% to $3.96 for fiscal year 2026 from $3.67 for fiscal year 2025;Net income increased 5% to $8.11 million for the current quarter from $7.72 million for the preceding quarter and decreased 4% from $8.45 million for the comparable quarter one year ago;Net income increased 7% to $31.17 million for the 2026 fiscal year from $29.16 million for the 2025 fiscal year;Return on average equity ("ROE”) and return on average assets ("ROA”) for the current quarter were 11.72% and 1.56%, respectively;Net interest margin ("NIM”) for the current quarter increased to 3.96% from 3.85% for the preceding quarter and 3.82% for the comparable quarter one year ago; andThe efficiency ratio for the current quarter was 53.94% compared to 53.40% for the preceding quarter and 53.18% for the comparable quarter one year ago. Balance Sheet Highlights:Total assets increased slightly, less than 1%, from the prior quarter and increased 3% year-over-year;Net loans receivable increased 2% from the prior quarter and increased 4% year-over-year;Total deposits increased slightly, less than 1%, from the prior quarter and increased 3% year-over-year;Total shareholders’ equity increased 1% from the prior quarter and increased 5% year-over-year; 40,395 shares of common stock were repurchased during the current quarter for $1.85 million;Non-performing assets to total assets ratio was 0.42% at September 30, 2026, compared to 0.43% at June 30, 2026, and 0.23% at September 30, 2025;Book and tangible book (non-GAAP) values per common share increased to $35.51 and $33.54, respectively, at September 30, 2026; andLiquidity (both on-balance sheet and off-balance sheet) remained strong at September 30, 2026, with only $5 million in borrowings and additional secured borrowing line capacity of $810 million available through the Federal Home Loan Bank ("FHLB”) and the Federal Reserve. Operating Results Operating revenue (net interest income before the provision for credit losses plus non-interest income) for the current quarter increased 5% to $22.79 million from $21.79 million for the preceding quarter and increased 1% from $22.49 million for the comparable quarter one year ago. The increase in operating revenue compared to the preceding quarter was primarily due to an increase in interest income on loans receivable, and to a lesser extent, an increase in non-interest income. These increases in operating revenue were partially offset by a decrease in interest income on interest-bearing deposits in banks, and to a lesser extent, an increase in interest expense. Operating revenue increased 6%, to $87.34 million for the 2026 fiscal year from $82.55 million for the 2025 fiscal year, primarily due to increases in interest income on loans receivable and interest income on interest-bearing deposits in banks, and a decrease in interest expense. These increases in operating revenue for the fiscal year were partially offset by decreases in interest income on investment securities and net BOLI earnings. Net interest income increased $857,000 or 5%, to $19.66 million for the current quarter from $18.81 million for the preceding quarter and increased $1.27 million, or 7%, from $18.40 million for the comparable quarter one year ago. The increase in net interest income compared to the preceding quarter was primarily due to an $11.46 million increase in the average interest-earning assets, a nine-basis point increase in the weighted average yield on interest-bearing assets and, to a lesser extent, a one-basis point decrease in the weighted average cost of interest-bearing liabilities. Net interest income for the 2026 fiscal year increased $5.46 million, or 8%, to $75.66 million from $70.20 million for the 2025 fiscal year, primarily due to an $89.24 million increase in average interest-earning assets and a 17-basis point decrease in the weighted average cost of interest-bearing liabilities. Timberland’s NIM for the current quarter increased to 3.96% from 3.85% for the preceding quarter and from 3.82% for the comparable quarter one year ago. The NIM for the current quarter was increased by approximately two basis points due to the collection of $94,000 in pre-payment penalties, non-accrual interest, and late fees, and the accretion of $8,000 of the fair value discount on acquired loans. The NIM for the preceding quarter was increased by approximately two basis points due to the collection of $82,000 in pre-payment penalties, non-accrual interest, and late fees, and the accretion of $8,000 of the fair value discount on acquired loans. The NIM for the comparable quarter one year ago was increased by approximately two basis points due to the collection of $102,000 in pre-payment penalties, non-accrual interest, and late fees, and the accretion of $11,000 of the fair value discount on acquired loans. Timberland’s NIM expanded to 3.87% for fiscal year 2026 from 3.76% for fiscal year 2025. A $475,000 provision for credit losses on loans was recorded for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. The provision was primarily due to loan portfolio growth and changes in the composition of the loan portfolio. This compares to a $600,000 provision for credit losses on loans for the preceding quarter and a $213,000 provision for credit losses on loans for the comparable quarter one year ago. Non-interest income increased $134,000, or 4%, to $3.12 million for the current quarter from $2.99 million for the preceding quarter and decreased $971,000, or 24%, from $4.09 million for the comparable quarter one year ago. The increase in non-interest income compared to the preceding quarter was primarily due to a $99,000 increase in BOLI net earnings and smaller increases in several other categories. Non-interest income for the 2026 fiscal year decreased by 5%, to $11.68 million from $12.35 million for the 2025 fiscal year. The decrease in non-interest income compared to the prior year periods was primarily the result of a $1.04 million BOLI death benefit claim recorded in the comparable quarter one year ago. Total operating (non-interest) expenses for the current quarter increased $652,000, or 6%, to $12.29 million from $11.64 million for the preceding quarter and increased $331,000, or 3%, from $11.96 million for the comparable quarter one year ago. The increase in operating expenses compared to the preceding quarter was primarily due to increases in salary and employee benefits expense and ATM and debit card processing expense and smaller decreases and increases in several other expense categories. The efficiency ratio for the current quarter was 53.94% compared to 53.40% for the preceding quarter and 53.18% for the comparable quarter one year ago. For the 2026 fiscal year, operating expenses increased $1.63 million, or 4%, to $47.02 million from $45.39 million for the 2025 fiscal year. The efficiency ratio for the 2026 fiscal year improved to 53.83% from 54.98% for the 2025 fiscal year. The provision for income taxes for the current quarter increased $32,000, or 2%, to $1.96 million from $1.93 million for the preceding quarter, primarily due to higher taxable income. Timberland’s effective income tax rate was 19.5% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to 20.0% for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, and 18.1% for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. Timberland’s effective income tax rate was 19.9% for fiscal year 2026 compared to 19.5% for fiscal year 2025. Balance Sheet Management Total assets increased $2.97 million, or less than 1%, during the quarter to $2.06 billion at September 30, 2026, from $2.06 billion at June 30, 2026, and increased $51.01 million, or 3%, from $2.01 billion one year ago. The increase during the quarter was primarily due to an increase in net loans receivable, which was partially offset by decreases in total cash and cash equivalents and investment securities. Liquidity Timberland has continued to maintain a strong liquidity position, both on-balance sheet and off-balance sheet. Liquidity, as measured by the sum of cash and cash equivalents, CDs held for investment, and available for sale investment securities, was 18.5% of total liabilities at September 30, 2026, compared to 19.3% at June 30, 2026, and 18.8% one year ago. Timberland also had secured borrowing line capacity of $810 million available through the FHLB and the Federal Reserve at September 30, 2026. With a strong and diversified deposit base, only 20% of Timberland’s deposits were uninsured or uncollateralized at September 30, 2026. (Note: This calculation excludes public deposits that are fully collateralized.) Loans Net loans receivable increased $30.60 million, or 2%, during the quarter to $1.53 billion at September 30, 2026, from $1.50 billion at June 30, 2026, and increased $62.66 million, or 4%, from $1.46 billion at September 30, 2025. The increase during the quarter was primarily due to an $18.19 million increase in multi-family loans, a $6.33 million increase in one- to four-family loans, a $3.12 million increase in land loans, a $2.04 million increase in commercial business loans, a $1.03 million increase in construction and land development loans, and smaller increases in several other loan categories. These increases were partially offset by a $1.85 million increase in the undisbursed portion of construction loans in process and smaller changes in several other loan categories. articles.title: Morgan Stanley’s Wilson sees one final sell-off before US stock correction ends
articles.description: Wilson’s roadmap (posted earlier this week) implies near-term downside for semiconductors and AI-linked credit, alongside a buy-the-dip setup for early-cycle sectors once the catalysts clear. That makes AI-linked debt issuance and data centre credit spreads key gauges to watch over the coming weeks. There’s also a possible two-stage dollar trade, though this is editorial interpretation rather than Morgan Stanley’s view. A final risk-off shock could lift the US dollar on safe-haven demand. If that stress pushes the Fed toward easing, it could also mark a peak in dollar strength. Higher energy prices tied to the Iran conflict remain a risk to the timeline, since they add to the tightening pressure Wilson describes. --- Morgan Stanley thinks the stock correction has one more leg down in it, and that the stress which delivers it may also bring the Fed to the rescue. Summary: Wilson says the equity correction that began in June is in its final stages He sees tactical S&P 500 downside to 7,100-7,200, then a year-end target of 8,000 AI concerns are expected to peak in three to four weeks as debt supply is absorbed, and chips could fall another 10% to 15% Morgan Stanley sees the midterms as a hurdle that markets typically benefit from clearing Wilson calls liquidity the key catalyst: financial conditions are near 2018 levels and close to 2022 severity, which risks forcing a Fed reversal Chips, financials, consumer cyclicals and autos are seen leading any recovery Morgan Stanley’s Mike Wilson believes the US equity correction that began in June is in its final stages. He expects markets may need one last sell-off before a sustained recovery, with three catalysts set to determine when the bottom arrives. Wilson, the bank’s chief US equity strategist, sees tactical downside for the S&P 500 to between 7,100 and 7,200, slightly below its 200-day moving average, before a rebound towards his year-end target of 8,000. He argues that much of the damage has already been done beneath the surface of the headline index. About 60% of Russell 3000 stocks are down more than 20% since the correction began, and in semiconductors the figure is 96%. The first catalyst is artificial intelligence. Morgan Stanley expects investor concerns over AI to peak over the next three to four weeks as markets absorb a sharp increase in related debt issuance. Those concerns include returns on capital, funding needs, widening credit spreads on data centre bonds and local opposition to new facilities. The bank’s strategists said semiconductors could fall a further 10% to 15% before finding support around mid-November. The second is the US midterm elections. Morgan Stanley sees the vote as a hurdle that markets benefit from clearing, rather than a lasting threat. It notes that the S&P 500 has historically gained about 17% on average in the 12 months after a midterm election. Wilson regards the third catalyst, liquidity, as the most important. The Federal Reserve has resumed rate increases and roughly halved the pace of its balance sheet growth, while higher energy prices add further pressure. In Wilson’s view, markets are effectively tightening financial conditions on the Fed’s behalf, and those conditions have now tightened to a degree comparable with 2018 and nearly as severe as 2022. That could slow growth and help bring inflation down. He warned, however, that it may also generate enough financial stress to force the Fed to reverse course before inflation is fully contained. Wilson sees opportunities as these catalysts resolve. Sentiment is neutral and third-quarter earnings growth is running near 27%. He expects early-cycle groups that have lagged, including chips, financials, consumer cyclicals and autos, to lead any recovery, with semiconductors offering the most rebound potential. The main risk to the view is timing: a slower resolution of any catalyst would push the expected bottom further out. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.title: Cobre Limited (ASX:CBE) September 2026 Quarterly Investor Briefing Presentation
articles.description: Cobre Limited (ASX:CBE) reported copper recovery of 78%, cathode production of 818t and positive EBITDA of +US$0.5m for the September 2026 quarter in its presentation dated 30 October 2026. The presentation outlines operating progress at Sierra Atacama in Chile, subsequent steps to secure control and additional feed, and a staged expansion pathway subject to studies, permitting, financing and Board approval. Sierra Atacama operations and ownership Copper recovery increased from 66% in March and 70% in June to 78%. September cathode production was 305t. A geotechnical review briefly paused some mining faces; surveying has been completed, with those faces scheduled to return during the December quarter. A new cathode plates overhaul was completed in August 2026, restoring cathode quality to ~99.98% purity. July production was affected by off-specification cathode. Third-party ore tolling began in September, with benefits expected to build into December. Following quarter-end, Cobre secured 62.86% control of Sierra Atacama on 12 October. The presentation outlined organic growth to 75% ownership through spending on the project. On 21 October, Cobre secured ~150kt of ENAMI oxide ore within 55km, in addition to completed third-party ore transactions. The presentation stated that third-party ore can add ~ 300t of cathode equivalent per month, with leaching taking 60-70 days and benefits expected in the December quarter. Exploration and staged expansion Cobre outlined a 40,000m resource programme comprising ~15,000m RC and ~25,000m diamond drilling. The first diamond hole reached 986.9m. Visual sulphides were observed at depth, qualified as visual estimates only. A total of 571 samples had been submitted, with assays expected in mid-November, towards a maiden JORC resource by the March Quarter. The expansion pathway comprises Stage 1 restoration and optimisation to ~18 ktpa, Stage 2 installation of a second SX line and additional electrowinning to ~25 ktpa, and a Stage 3 open-pit case of up to ~50 ktpa following the 40,000m programme. These are indicative target capacities only, subject to studies, permitting, financing and Board approval, and are not production guidance. In Botswana, the Ngami ISCR well-field was completed, comprising six production and four monitoring wells. At Okavango, with Sinomine, ~1.6km of a ~3km drilling programme had been completed. Financial position and funding For Q1 FY27, covering July-September 2026, Cobre reported revenue of ~US$11.8m and positive EBITDA of +US$0.5m, its second consecutive quarter of positive EBITDA. September EBITDA was +US$974k. The presentation reported pro forma cash of ~A$90m, including A$18m Tranche 2 in early October. It identified ~US$12m to take 62.86% control of Sierra Atacama. Reported debt was US$32.2m, comprising US$16.0m of financing debt, US$11.0m of trade creditors and US$5.2m of other or legacy obligations. Financing debt was described as structured and scheduled at ~US$600k/month. Cobre was assessing early repayments, while a discounted settlement was progressing towards a creditors' meeting on 26 November 2026. The capital programme identifies ~US$8m for exploration drilling and ~US$20-25m for SX-EW refurbishment and expansion, with studies being completed. The presentation describes this capital programme as fully funded from the A$90m capital raise. The exploration programme comprises 40,000m in CY2026, with a similar programme planned for CY2027. December-quarter priorities Priorities include converting EBITDA into positive cash flow, increasing third-party and low-cost feed, restoring head grade, awarding the Stage 1 tender by December quarter-end, submitting the Stage 2 DIA, and advancing open-pit planning and permitting. *To view Cobre Company Presentation, please visit: https://abnnewswire.net/lnk/4LFUVKRB Editorial Note: This media release has been independently prepared by ABN Newswire editorial staff based on Cobre Limited's Company Presentation. It is intended as an editorial summary of information disclosed in that report and should be read in conjunction with Cobre's full ASX announcement. All financial, operational and post-reporting-period information in this editorial has been sourced from the Company's report. Cobre Limited Martin Holland E: info@cobre.com.au WWW: www.cobre.com.au

Varun Beverages Q3 Revenue Up 33.2% to ₹66,075.6 Mn
articles.description: Varun Beverages Limited (VBL) announced its financial results for Q3 and 9M CY2026. Q3 revenue surged 33.2% YoY to Rs. 66,075.6 million, driven by a 28.7% increase in consolidated sales volume to 354.4 million cases. India volumes grew 22.5% and international volumes 39.9%, including 15.3 million cases from the Twizza acquisition in South Africa. Consolidated beverage realization per case improved by 2.2%. Gross margin declined 334 bps to 53.1% due to higher packaging material costs and geopolitical disruptions. EBITDA increased 25.1% YoY to Rs. 14,267.1 million, while PAT rose 13.5% to Rs. 8,305.9 million. For 9M 2026, revenue grew 23.3% YoY to Rs. 218,145.5 million, EBITDA by 19.9% to Rs. 52,745.8 million, and PAT by 15.5% to Rs. 32,023.0 million. VBL also reported the acquisition of business from Devyani Food Industries (Kenya) Limited for USD 32 million.
